FRAUD-RISK QUESTIONNAIRE
Client: Harbour & Pine Joinery Ltd    Year ended 30 June 2026
Completed by: R. Okafor, finance director    Reviewed by: audit senior, 14 August 2026

Q1. Who is responsible for preventing and detecting fraud?
The board. Day to day, the finance director; payments over $10,000 need a second director's approval.

Q2. Are you aware of any actual, suspected or alleged fraud affecting the entity?
No allegations by staff, customers or regulators this year.

Q3. Has the entity been the victim of fraud, a scam or theft during the year or since? If so, describe each
case and its cost to the entity.
Yes, twice.
(a) Payment scam. On 11 March 2026 accounts payable received a phishing email that appeared to come from our
timber supplier, Northgate Timber, giving new bank details. Invoice 4471 was paid to the new account. The real
supplier chased the invoice three weeks later. Loss: $48,200. The bank recovered nothing; the insurer declined
the claim because the policy excludes payments made on false instructions.
(b) Theft. A laptop and a site tablet were stolen from the warehouse office on 2 June 2026. Insurance paid the
replacement cost less the $500 excess.

Q4. What did you change as a result?
Changes to supplier bank details are now confirmed by a call to a number already on file (since April 2026).
Laptops are kept in a locked cabinet overnight.
--- page ---
FRAUD-RISK QUESTIONNAIRE (continued)

Q5. Do any employees have incentives or pressures that could lead to fraudulent reporting?
Sales staff earn a bonus on orders booked; the bonus is paid on cash received, not on orders.

Q6. Is there a whistleblowing procedure?
Yes, a line to the chair of the board. No reports this year.

Q7. Are there related parties that management controls outside the entity?
The managing director owns the premises; rent of $54,000 a year is charged at market rate.

Q8. Has the entity received any communication from regulators about fraud or non-compliance?
No.

Signed: R. Okafor, finance director, 12 August 2026
